title: Loop back: debugging a wrong decision
idea: LOOP. No new concept. Review the debugging skill from Unit 32 - name the decision bug and say how to fix it.

exercises.prompt: A grade chain checks 'score >= 80' before 'score >= 90', so a 95 gets 'B'. What is the bug?
options: Branch order - the strict test should come first
exercises.explanation: Checking 90 first fixes it. (Review of order bugs.)

exercises.prompt: Rule 'at least 21' coded as 'age > 21' rejects exactly 21. What is the bug and fix?
exercises.explanation: 'At least' includes the boundary, so >=. (Review of boundary bugs.)

exercises.prompt: A chain handles only scores 50+ with no else, so a 30 prints nothing. The fix is...
options: Add an else (or elif) for the lower scores
exercises.explanation: The missing case needs its own branch. (Review of missing cases.)

exercises.prompt: 'accept y or yes' coded as 'answer == "y" and answer == "yes"' never accepts. The fix is...
exercises.explanation: One value cannot be both, so 'or' is needed. (Review of the and/or swap.)

exercises.prompt: A number check from input() always fails because 'if age == 18' compares text to a number. The fix is...
options: Convert with int() so age is a number
exercises.explanation: int(input(...)) makes the comparison numeric. (Review of the type bug.)

exercises.prompt: The wrong output tells you which branch ran, which helps you find the faulty condition.
exercises.explanation: Output is a clue pointing at the branch to inspect. (Review of reading output.)

exercises.prompt: 'Yes' is rejected by 'if answer == "yes"'. What is the cause?
exercises.explanation: == on strings is case-exact. Accept both forms with 'or'. (Review of case bugs.)

exercises.prompt: A condition written with a single '=' instead of '==' is wrong because...
options: = assigns, but a condition needs == to compare
exercises.explanation: A test needs the comparison ==, not the assignment =. (Review of = vs ==.)

exercises.prompt: Order the steps to debug a wrong decision.
blocks: Pick an input with a known correct answer
Fix the condition that is wrong
exercises.explanation: Known input, trace, read the branch, fix. (Review of the debugging routine.)

exercises.prompt: Two separate ifs both print a label for the same number. The fix for 'one label only' is...
options: Chain them with elif so only one runs
exercises.explanation: elif makes the branches exclusive. (Review of separate-if vs elif.)
